title: DDS Core — shared definitions
description: Building blocks every other DDS schema refers to. Field names are camelCase.

id.description: Stable identifier: upper-case segments joined by hyphens, optionally a lower-case dotted suffix for a part of something (a check of a rule). Examples: DDS-PARAM-003, DDS-PARAM-003.present, JOB-CREATE-FAMILY, OBS-000123, Q-NEST-004.

ref.description: The id of another DDS item. The prefix tells the reader what kind of item it is (see spec/01-information-types.md).

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 date-time, or a plain date when the time is unknown.

actor.description: Who did something: a person, an AI, or a script/tool.

name.description: Person's name or role-holder; AI model id; script or tool name.

role.description: The role they acted in, e.g. 'standards owner', 'reviewer', 'family author'.

version.description: Model or tool version, when kind is ai or script.

basis.description: Where a rule or outcome stands on evidence. unset = nobody has said yet. borrowed = taken from a framework default or another layer, not yet checked for this owner. seen = evidenced in the owner's own work (harvested, observed, drafted by AI) but not confirmed. confirmed = a named person with authority has confirmed it. AI may raise an item to 'seen' at most; only a person makes it 'confirmed'.

lifecycle.description: Whether an item is in use. draft = written, not applied. active = applied in runs and checks. retired = kept for history, not applied.

severity.description: How strict a rule or check is. must = a failure blocks. should = a failure is reported. may = advice.

confidentiality.description: Who may see the item or source. confidential material (client files, models, recordings) never goes into a public repository; reference it by path and hash instead.

evidence.description: What an item rests on: observations, sources, runs or reviews, each with an optional note.

confirmation.description: The person who confirmed an item, and when. Required when basis is 'confirmed'.

source.description: The told source (interview, email, minutes) where the confirmation was given.

created.description: Who made an item and how.

method.description: told = from a person; found = extracted from an artefact; documented = taken from a written protocol/video; distilled = derived by analysis; authored = written directly; imported = copied from another pack.

location.description: Where a file or resource is. Paths are relative to the pack root unless absolute or a URI.

extensions.description: Adapter- or tool-specific fields, namespaced by the adapter id, e.g. { "revit-families": { ... } }. Core readers ignore what they don't know.
